 In 2026, Bruno Fernandes ranks first for each of chances created (104), open play chances created (80), big chances created (27), successful final third passes (531), passes/crosses played into the opposition box (289), and through balls (29). He’s averaging 3.8 chances created per 90 minutes under Michael Carrick, the best by any United player under a single manager in the league since 2003-04 (min. 1,000 mins played).

 Fernandes 'as good as ever' published at 16:24 GMT 16:24 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 It seems all is rosy again between Michael Carrick and his captain Bruno Fernandes.
 After the Portugal midfielder criticised the manager and his tactics following the 4-1 hammering by Como in the Champions League, Fernandes was left on the bench for the home loss to Bournemouth but returned a week later for the defeat by Chelsea.
 He did score a retaken penalty to spark Manchester United's remarkable comeback against Roma in Europe earlier this week, and said there have been "a lot of lies" reported about his relationship with Carrick.
 The 32-year-old rejected the notion there had been "clear-the-air talks" between the pair - something which had been confirmed by club sources.
 "I think his actions, the way he's played and how he dealt with even retaking the penalty and frame of mind he was in for that, tells [you] everything," Carrick said.
 "Bruno's as good as ever."
 2 9 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Circus tent or a Premier League title?' published at 16:23 GMT 16:23 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Paul Robinson 
Former Leeds goalkeeper on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 Manchester United were and possibly still are the biggest football club in Europe. How did they get there? Because of the success on the football pitch.
 They're talking about building this new stadium. If you asked every single Manchester United fan - do you want a new stadium which looks like a circus tent or a Premier League title
 I'll tell you what they'd take, a title, and that's what they want.
 The eyes have been taken away from the football pitch. They're not that team on the grass. 
 The people that support United, not the tourists, the hardcore Manchester United fans, they want to see their team being successful.
 It is not rocket science. If the team is successful, the team wins trophies, then everything else goes hand in hand.

 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox have just taken their seats in the stand.
 The pair glance over at the green and gold protest.

 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 'We don't want a new stadium, we want new owners'
 Those are the words emblazoned on a banner inside Old Trafford as the green and gold balloons are waved by those fans participating in the protest.

 Green and gold Man Utd fan protest published at 16:21 GMT 16:21 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Chief Football News Reporter at Old Trafford 
 Manchester United fans have been encouraged to bring green and gold 'balloons, scarves and shirts' to today's game by six fan groups who are trying to increase the pressure on the club's owners.
 The 'Reclaim Our Colours' initiative is felt to be a visual way of expressing unhappiness at the present situation.
 In a release to publicise the plans, organisers have highlighted the following issues:
 - Against the ownership
 - Against demolishing Old Trafford
 - Against the disrespect being shown to match-goers
 - Against the attack on traditional fan culture
 - Against the decline in standards throughout the club
 - Against the compounding debt
 They are also calling for supporters not to buy drinks inside the stadium.
 56 11 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Why is it acceptable?' published at 16:20 GMT 16:20 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Nedum Onuoha 
Former Man City defender on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 There is so much noise around Manchester United at the moment - which is valid. Noise coming from fans, former players and pundits about the general running of the football club.
 But they could potentially be bottom of the Premier League in the middle of November. This is with a manager that yes, did well for them last season but why is it acceptable?
 You can say the transfer window didn't go the way they wanted and that they've got injuries but are they the third-worst squad in the Premier League right now? I don't think that they are.
 As a consequence of that significant decisions and consequences need to be made about the manager.
 29 34 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Carrick has made a lot of mistakes' published at 16:19 GMT 16:19 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Julien Laurens 
French football journalist on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 In his time at the club Ruben Amorim was never 18th in the Premier League - neither was Eric Ten Haag, neither was Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.
 All of them were sacked in better positions, with more points than where Michael Carrick is at right now.
 I think he has made a lot of mistakes with this team going from third last season to this season. I think he needed a bit more authority this year from pre-season. He's not an interim coach anymore, he needs to be the number one.
 People can tell me that he's different to those other coaches and he'll turn things around but for now I'm not seeing it.
 51 28 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 16:18 GMT 16:18 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Tommy Smith 
Former Middlesbrough defender on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 The expectation around Manchester United needs to change.
 Where they are now in the Premier League set up they are not a top four side. In terms of the way they play, the players that they have they are just not.
 When it comes to the club, the stadium, the size of the club - they are the biggest club in the world. That does not autmotically dictate where you are in the division. I just don't see Manchester United as a club competing for top four anymore.

 Why would Emery want to go to Man Utd? published at 16:16 GMT 16:16 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Chris Sutton 
Former Blackburn striker on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 Why would Unai Emery want to [be Man Utd manager]? He is a brilliant manager and coach, all about detail.
 Why would he want to touch them at this moment in time?
 It's not to say he couldn't achieve something there, of course he could.
 They've been through so many managers and coaches. When he see's that, I don't necessarily want to call it a failure, but, failure from high-profile guys in the game, with what he's achieved at Villa, why would he want to go there?

 Huge game for Man Utd published at 16:12 GMT 16:12 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Chief Football News Reporter at Old Trafford 
 So, now we know.
 If Manchester United lose today, they will spend the next two weeks second bottom of the Premier League. If they draw, they will be third bottom.
 Victory today would edge them up to 15th or 16th.
 That wouldn't be good but it would leave them two points behind Aston Villa, Newcastle and Tottenham. They would only be six points behind Chelsea, who are fifth.
 It would mean United could look up, rather than in fear of where they are.
 51 39 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 16:10 GMT 16:10 GMT 
 It's all over in the 2pm matches, here are the results:
 Brighton 2-0 Brentford 
 Crystal Palace 1-3 Liverpool 
 Ipswich Town 1-2 Bournemouth 
 Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea 
 And here is how it leaves things in the Premier League table. Manchester United aiming to get out of the bottom three and Aston Villa bidding for a place in the top 10 before the international break.

 Villa's Old Trafford record not great published at 16:08 GMT 16:08 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Matthew Hobbs 
BBC Sport journalist 
 Since beating Manchester City in October, Villa have been knocked out of the League Cup at Bournemouth, drawn with Fulham and lost at the Nou Camp, so a rare away win in this fixture would be timely.
 Villa won their first Premier League match against United under Unai Emery in November 2022, but that came at home. Emery has never won in nine career attempts at Old Trafford, losing on all five visits with Villa.
 Now would be the perfect time to arrest that record as he approaches a 200th Premier League game as a manager.
 The 55-year-old will become the fifth Spaniard to reach the milestone after Rafael Benitez, Roberto Martinez, Pep Guardiola, and Mikel Arteta.
 Benitez and Arteta's 200th matches also came against United, and both avoided defeats.
 25 10 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Greatest club in the world' published at 16:06 GMT 16:06 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Chief Football News Reporter at Old Trafford 
 We've just had the first reading of the teams from the stadium announcer.
 He finished off by saying 'let's get behind the reds' and called Manchester United 'the greatest club in the world'.
 I know there is a PR element to that and it is his job to create positivity but I saw Crystal Palace concede a third goal and my first thought was 'Manchester United can't be bottom during the international break'.
 That is just mad.
 38 74 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Emery deserves everything at Villa' published at 16:03 GMT 16:03 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Tommy Smith 
Former Middlesbrough Town defender on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 People are saying they would love to see Unai Emery at Manchester United but at Aston Villa he has got total control and would he get that at United? There is an argument to say no he wouldn't.
 Emery deserves everything he gets at Villa - a new contract is a smack in the face to other clubs to say 'this is our manager' and he deserves it. What he has done consistently over the last few years is transition a playing squad to get the absolute maximum out of those players.
 The players that have left the club in the last few years - Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Emi Martinez - significant players that have left and he continues to churn out results and performances.
 64 9 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 200 up for Emery published at 16:00 GMT 16:00 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 This will be Aston Villa boss Unai Emery’s 200th Premier League game in charge. He’s the fifth Spaniard to reach this milestone after Rafael Benítez, Roberto Martínez, Pep Guardiola, and Mikel Arteta, with Benítez’s (2-0 win) and Arteta’s (1-1 draw) 200th games also coming against Man Utd.
 And what a job he has done.
 Image source, Getty Images 
 57 8 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Emery to United? Doesn't look like it published at 15:57 GMT 15:57 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Football is funny sometimes, isn't it.
 Manchester United are in a dire situation and, to get themselves out of trouble, must beat Unai Emery's Aston Villa. A side who also had a poor start to the season but seem to be turning things around under one of the most respected coaches in the game.
 A coach that many United fans would like to see in their own dugout and who has been heavily linked with the job, should United choose to part ways with Michael Carrick.
 It looks like that won't happen given what Guillem Balague has just said.
 But it feels like the two clubs are heading in complete opposite directions.
 48 9 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Emery close to new Villa deal published at 15:54 GMT 15:54 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Guillem Balague 
Spanish football journalist 
 Aston Villa head coach Unai Emery is close to agreeing a contract extension at the club - which will hand him even more responsibility for long-term development.
 The Villa boss held talks with the hierarchy on Wednesday to discuss the club's future, with all parties keen on extending his time at Villa Park.
 Emery would relish the opportunity to play an even bigger role in developing the club for the long term, with talks ongoing about the fine details, the finances, and the length of the new deal.
 The plan is to announce the new contract once all details have been agreed.
 60 9 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 No international break plans for Carrick published at 15:51 GMT 15:51 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Chief Football News Reporter at Old Trafford 
 Manchester United's hierarchy are expected to assess the situation at the club during the forthcoming international break.
 They committed to giving Michael Carrick and his players a chance to turn the situation around after the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth a fortnight ago, since when they performed well in the first-half against Chelsea, but lost, and badly in the first half against Roma but won, thrillingly, in the Champions League.
 For all the debate about Carrick's future, he has no special plans for the couple of weeks between today and the trip to Liverpool.
 "We're just carrying on as normal," said Carrick.
 "International breaks are
always a time, when talking about the players that aren't going away
and for the staff, to re-energise and freshen up.
 "There is an element of that, but I don't
really need it. I'm fine as I am."
